title: Engine actions
source: A fixture for the audits: the IDE actions the workflow and Quarto lessons use.
summary: Reformat a messy script, render a Quarto report, switch to the visual editor and back, start a new Quarto document and press the pipe shortcut.

steps.title: Setup: library(dplyr)
steps.explain: dplyr is attached. The tidyverse from the other fixture isn't: R restarted when the lesson changed.

steps.title: Reformat a messy script

ide.editor_text:
# A script written in a hurry
fast <- trips |>
  filter(duration_min < 10, bike_type == "electric") |>
  select(trip_id, start_station, duration_min)
km_to_miles <- function(km) {
  km * 0.621371
}

runs.purpose: reformat the whole script with Air

steps.explain: Air put spaces around operators, one pipe step on each line, and the function's body on its own line.

steps.title: Render a report
steps.explain: Quarto ran the code chunk and wrote report.html, which the Viewer shows.

steps.title: The visual editor

runs.purpose: switch report.qmd to the visual editor
switch back to the source editor
runs.task: Switch back to the source editor.

steps.explain: The visual editor shows the document as it will look; the source editor shows its markdown.

steps.title: A new Quarto document

runs.task: Start a new Quarto document with File › New File › Quarto Document…, then press Create.

steps.explain: RStudio opened an untitled Quarto document with a title and an HTML format.

steps.title: The pipe shortcut

runs.purpose: type the pipe with its shortcut
runs.task: In the new document, press Ctrl+Shift+M.

steps.explain: Ctrl+Shift+M types the pipe, `|>`, wherever the cursor is.
